content.thinking:
I should check the sandbox directory listing and the glow kit to confirm the working path before proceeding. Now I'm sketching the design for the kitsune: a nine-tailed, high-fantasy anime fox standing on four legs, somewhat larger than a real fox, with a shoulder height around 0.9 m and body length near 1.3 m.

I'm fleshing out the full design: nine fanned tails with floating foxfire orbs around their tips, a cream-white coat with crimson kumadori-style markings, gold ornaments (forehead crest, neck ring with bell, shide-paper ribbon, gold tail bands), and a resting pose with legs apart and jaw separated. For the palette I'm picking cream-white, crimson-orange, lavender-blue inner ears, warm gold, and a blue-teal/violet spirit-flame glow, with the flame orbs built from glowing teardrop shapes layered with SVG flame textures. I'm also planning the tail rig — nine chains of five joints each plus the body skeleton, keeping the total under 160 joints — and working out how to fan the tails in an arc from their root position at the base of the spine.

Now I'm figuring out the yaw spread for each tail (about ±68° across the fan) with the center tail angled higher and the outer ones lower, varying tail length and thickness with a tapered radius profile for a fluffy pointed tip. I'm deciding on a cream fur color with a red band and flame-colored glowing tip for each tail, plus a gold ring ornament near the base, and estimating the fur card budget (roughly 540 cards across all nine tails) to keep the triangle count reasonable.

Then I'm moving to the body: laying out a spine chain from hips to chest to neck to head with specific joint coordinates for a proud standing posture, aiming for a shoulder height around 0.8m and total height near 1.25m including raised ears and tail fan. I'm sketching the body proportions as slim and elegant, with an elliptical radius sweep along the spine for the rump and chest.

Rather than a single continuous sweep, I'm deciding to split the body into a spine sweep for the torso and a separate neck sweep that overlaps and buries into the chest to avoid a visible seam, keeping the root joint at the hips with tails parented there. I'm also starting to define the coat paint palette, setting up cel-shaded colors for white and red markings with lavender-tinted shadows.

I'm settling on a kitsune design: an elegant white/cream fox with crimson kumadori-style face markings, red-tipped ears and tail, and red socks on the legs, aiming for a high-fantasy anime look with gold ornaments. Now I'm working out how to paint the saddle markings on the back using swirl stripe patterns in crimson against the cream base coat.

I'm planning crimson arabesque swirl decals (tomoe/flame-style) mirrored on both flanks and haunches to add visual richness, and designing slender fox legs with dark crimson gradient "stockings" fading toward the lower leg.

For the front legs, I'm plotting a three-segment chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw) with slightly oversized total segment length relative to the target distance to create a natural slight bend rather than a stiff straight line.

Now I'm working through the hind leg rig, considering a four-segment chain (hip, knee, hock, ball, toe) with specific segment lengths and figuring out the sole orientation so the toe sits flat against the floor.

Adding a sole option so the last segment lies flat pointing forward, with the foot/paw as that final floor-contact segment of the chain from shoulder through elbow, wrist, to toe base.

I'm reconsidering the limb as four segments: shoulder-elbow, elbow-wrist, wrist-ball, and ball-toe, with the final segment's "sole" lying flat against the ground while the ball point sits slightly elevated at the heel position. That gives lengths roughly 0.3, 0.28, 0.12, and 0.1 for a more natural digitigrade stance.

Checking the total span from shoulder to ball against the sum of segment lengths, the leg comes out nearly straight, which seems fine with a slight wrist bend for realism. For bend directions, since the sole constraint fixes the last joint, I only need bend hints for the elbow and wrist -- elbow bending backward, wrist bending forward -- though I'm not fully confident in the sign convention, so I'll test it visually with a bones preview. Now I'm working out the hind leg similarly, with the hip as root and the toe target on the floor, figuring out the hock's backward bend direction.

For the leg meshes, I'm planning to sweep tapered cylinders along each joint chain, with thinner radii for the fox's slim legs and thicker ellipsoid masses added at the haunch and shoulder for visual bulk. For the paws, I'll sweep a rounded cap along the ball-to-toe segment and add small dark claw spikes projecting forward.

Now I'm shifting to the head: a scaled skull sphere, tapered muzzle, dark nose sphere, separate upper and lower jaws, cheek fur tufts, and large triangular ears extruded with red tips, white/pink inner coloring, and a small ear ornament. I'm also considering eye decals on the skull surface with an amber or violet color choice.

For eye color, I'm settling on a warm gold iris ("#ffb21c") to contrast against the cooler teal-blue flames and cream-colored face. I'm orienting the head joint to face forward, positioning the skull center further out, and defining the skull's width, height, and length proportions before lofting a tapered muzzle shape from the skull front toward the nose.

Now I'm sweeping the upper and lower jaw shapes with tapering radii and round caps, adding small fang-like cones for teeth, and deciding to keep the mouth closed with just a slight gap so a fang peeks through. I'm also planning thin swept whiskers in cream/gold on each side of the muzzle, fur tuft cards on the cheeks, and a gold marking on the forehead.

I'm layering face markings as decals projected onto the skull and muzzle surfaces -- crimson kumadori-style lines above the eyes and a forehead tomoe -- placing the eyes afterward slightly raised above the marks, positioned on the sides of the skull but angled forward for that anime-style gaze. Now I'm sweeping the neck shape with a tapering radius and starting to add a fur ruff around it.

For accessories, I'm thinking a big fluffy white chest ruff made from scattered fur-tuft cards, plus a gold collar with hanging tassels and a bell, gold anklets on the front legs, gold rings along each tail, and a flowing red ribbon sash at the waist -- keeping the overall look elegant with a gold crescent-moon forehead crest and gilded ear tips rather than piling on too many ornaments.

I'm also adding a magatama bead necklace draped around the neck and chest using merged teal jade spheres, plus some swirling ribbon accents for extra kitsune flair. For the mystical element, I want floating foxfire orbs -- flame tips on each of the nine tails and a handful more hovering loosely around the fox's body, attached near the nearest joint so they move naturally while still keeping the lowest point of the model touching the floor.

Designing the flame shape itself...

I'm layering the flame in 3D with a smaller white-ish inner core, plus a few smaller side licks, building it as nested sweeps—outer teal-blue glow, inner pale cyan, white core—with curved spike shapes radiating around for extra flame detail, each with its own glow.

For color I'm leaning toward a violet-to-cyan-to-white palette for the foxfire flames, and planning for the tail tips to dissolve into flame with a crimson transition where the tail meets the fire.

I'm also considering adding scattered ember sparkle cards floating around the tails for extra atmosphere, using small glowing star or diamond shapes, while keeping the bounding box constraints in mind.

For the fur texture cards, I'm using simple flat-colored SVG shapes for the flame wisps to keep rendering safe, and designing tuft shapes as grey-white forms so they can be tinted by the coat paint at each location, letting the cream-to-red gradient along the tails come through naturally.

I'm now working out tail details like adding a gold ring band around each tail using a swept torus shape, figuring out the right radius by sampling the tail sweep's thickness at that point, and considering how to orient the ring using the correct frame so it wraps around properly rather than following the tangent direction.

Wrapping the gradient in cel shading so shadows get computed from the resolved paint, and making sure fur cards sample the same paint at their root. For scattering cards along each tail, I'm using surface scatter with a minimum distance and random generator, orienting cards along the tail tangent rather than the default downward flow direction.

Now I'm tallying up the total part count across body, legs, head, tails, floating flames, embers, and decor to stay safely under the 1000-part budget -- landing around 350.

Triangle counts also check out as fine, well under 60k. Now I'm moving to the skeleton structure, starting with the root "hips" joint and building the spine chain off of it, figuring out the right joint roles and parent relationships.

I'm laying out the body path from hips up through the spine to the chest, deciding on specific coordinates for each spine point, then working through how the tail chains should attach near the hip base with slightly varied positions so they don't overlap.

Continuing up the body, I'm laying out the neck chain from the chest toward the head base, then placing the head joint angled slightly forward and down, before defining the body's radius taper from a narrower rump to a fuller chest.

I'm reworking the proportions, setting shoulder height around 0.85 with spine at 0.72 so the back sits at 0.86 and belly at 0.58, giving reasonably long elegant legs. Now I'm placing the hip joint near the lower body and sizing the leg segments so their combined length reaches the floor from that root point.

For hind legs I'm positioning the hip and ball joints to allow a strong knee-forward, hock-back bend that stays consistent with the tail base location above. Then I'm starting on the fan of nine tails, defining a normalized parameter per tail to control their spread and yaw angle.

Still working out tail geometry: I'm thinking through pitch angles so the center tails sit more upright while outer ones flare lower, like a peacock fan arcing in a plane perpendicular to the back's direction, using a cone axis tilted up and back to compute each tail's direction vector.

Working out the curved bezier paths for each tail, so the tips swirl upward and outward slightly beyond the base splay direction.

With 9 tails at 5 joints each that's 45 joints, plus roughly 20 more for spine, neck, head, ears and legs, I'm landing around 80 joints total—well under the 160 budget, so I have room for extras like tassels. The tail tip orientation should follow the path's end tangent to get the flame-like curl right.

For the texturing I'm thinking tufted grey-white fur with crimson swirl bands and a gold ring on each tail, maybe a second red band for variety. For the body coat, I'll go with a cream base with crimson shoulder-mantle markings as decal swirls, and crimson sock gradients on the legs that darken toward the paws with a jagged zigzag edge.

For the ears, I'm picturing a dark crimson or black outer surface with a cream fur tuft inside, extruded as separate front/back faces so I can color the inner front panel cream or peachy and the outer back panel crimson with a reddish tip.

Now for facial markings, I'm designing a decal in SVG coordinates mapped onto the front of the head covering forehead, eyes, and muzzle—kumadori-style red sweeping lines from the eye corners back to the cheeks, plus a red flame or diamond shape with a gold center dot placed near the top of the forehead.

For body markings, I'm setting up flank decals using curling flame-like swirl strokes in crimson with gold accent dots, sized to fit the flank area and oriented for the left side of the body.

I'll mirror the design for the other side so both read symmetrically, then work out the gold ornaments: a forehead crest with a crescent shape and red gem, extruded onto the skull and oriented to face forward using the head's local axes.

For placement, I'm using surface raycasting on the skull to find the exact forehead position for the crest. Then for the neck, I'll add a gold collar ring at the neck base joint, built as a swept band around the loop with a possible hanging bell detail.

For decoration, I'm planning jade magatama beads distributed along the collar loop, a gold bell pendant hanging from a cord at the front, and three red tassels with card textures draped forward from the collar. I'll also add gold bangles swept as rings around the front leg joints.

Then I'm adding matching rings at the hind hocks and tail, small gold torus ear cuffs at each ear's lower edge with dangling tassel-and-bead charms, and finally a flowing crimson hagoromo ribbon with gold trim curving along the flanks and shoulders as a floating sheer membrane for dramatic effect.

For rigging the ribbons, I'm thinking each needs its own joint chain rather than rigid attachment to the neck bone, since a long floating ribbon spanning from collar to the tail region needs to bend naturally through space—so I'll set up something like a "ribbonL" and "ribbonR" chain parented to the spine, repurposing a tentacle-like joint role to let it sway independently.

Writing sweep geometry...

I should add leg feathering tufts at the forelegs, elbows, and hocks, plus chunky cheek ruff fur—maybe three curved cream spikes per side using cone shapes or swept bezier curves to get that anime-fox cheek tuft look.

For body fur, I'll scatter tuft cards across the body, neck/chest, and legs with varying density, reusing the same tuft textures with paint-based tinting so the tail and other fur can share assets but differ in color—leaning toward a Kitsune-style red/white palette like Yae Miko's fox form. Now onto designing the nose.

For the nose, I'll use a small dark crimson-plum sphere with a tiny highlight, plus an ink-colored mouth line swept along the muzzle. I'm deciding to keep the mouth mostly closed but add a slight 4-degree gap revealing a small pink tongue and hint of fangs, making sure the lower jaw sweep is thick enough to avoid any visible void. For construction order, I'll build from body to neck to head parts to decals, then define the head joint direction aiming slightly forward and down with local left/right/up vectors established.

Now I'm working out head geometry: a skull sphere offset forward from the head joint with specific x/y/z radii, sized a bit larger for a stylized anime-fox look relative to the body width. I'm sweeping the muzzle from the skull forward using a tapering radius function, and setting up a separate jaw joint positioned below and forward of the skull, aiming further forward and down to support the lower jaw sweep.

Still defining facial features...

Still defining ear geometry...

Since the normal flips with mirrored sides, I decide inner vs outer coloring using the z-component of the normal rather than which side it's on. For the ear geometry itself, I'm planning a flat extrude with fine bevel, large kitsune-style proportions, plus inner fluff and cream tufts near the base, with crimson tips and darker crimson on the outer back.

For the rest of the head I'm thinking through hinge joints at each ear base aiming upward, scattered neck/chest ruff cards, and eye placement computed from azimuth/elevation angles relative to the skull center, projecting decals along the hit normal with mirrored sizing. I'm leaning toward keeping eyes plain rather than glowing, to preserve the flat anime shading style, and now turning to positioning spirit flame effects.

Now I'm figuring out the floating foxfire orbs around the fox -- arranging roughly six of them in a ring at varying heights and angles at about 0.75m radius, each made of a sphere core plus flame sweep, parented to a dedicated "foxfire" joint attached to the hips rather than scattering them individually, while deciding to skip a connecting trail ring to keep things simple.

For embers and sparks I'm scattering small star-shaped glowing cards randomly around the tails and body using a frame-based card generator with randomized positions and directions, cross-faced for visibility, then adding two-layer flame wisp cards at each tail tip combining a violet outer teardrop, teal middle, and white inner glow for extra flame detail.

Now I'm layering the actual 3D flame body itself: a core sweep along a bezier curve with a teardrop radius profile, nesting an outer violet layer, a mid cyan-blue layer, and an inner near-white core at progressively smaller radii so each layer peeks through the one around it.

Since flat anime-style flames need layered flat colors rather than true 3D depth, I'm thinking crossed card planes with a layered SVG flame texture (violet outer, cyan mid, white core) could give that classic stylized fire look while still working in 3D.

I'll vary the flow direction laterally per flame for variety, with a gentle bend to curl the tips. I want the cards full-bright colored rather than textured dark, and I'm checking whether I can batch all flame cards into a single mesh call since each frame carries its own bone data.

I'll split into two separate card calls, one for the tail flames and one for the foxfire orb flames, plus a small teardrop sweep for the 3D core. For tail frame construction, I'm figuring out how to pull the bone-carrying point from the tail chain to build each frame correctly.

I'm reconsidering the tail tip shape — a sharply pointed cap would leave the flame looking disconnected, so I'll round the tip slightly (end radius ~0.035) so the fur and flame blend together more naturally.

For the crimson zigzag tips, I want the edge direction to follow the tail's local tangent at that point rather than a fixed axis, so each tail's fur teeth swing along its own perpendicular direction using position-based leveling off the path point and tangent near the tip.

Then I'm wrapping the fur edge in the cel shading function, and thinking about adding extra decoration: a gold ring near the red zigzag zone, maybe a thinner second ring lower down, plus a cuff near the tail base with slightly larger radius than the tail's sweep, using closed circular rings positioned along the chain at specific parameter values.

I'm importing the glow kit, then sketching out the fur tuft texture as an SVG leaf shape with a darker grey stroke down the center for texture, tinted by the paint color so greys stay neutral while picking up the base hue.

Then I'm designing the flame card's SVG: a layered violet-cyan-white curling flame shape with an S-curl tip, tracing the outer path from base to the twisting point at the top.

Now planning the remaining icons: a tiny sparkle star in white-cyan, a red tassel with a gold bead and hanging strands, and a magatama shape using curved bezier sweeps for jade beads strung along a neck loop with a larger central piece.

Writing SVG swirl paths...

Then I'm considering how the decal's standard material lighting might slightly mismatch the cel-shaded baked body paint, since the decal gets lit normally by scene lights while the body uses flat cel shading.

For the hind-thigh marking, I'm planning a separate spiral swirl decal on the haunches, projecting it onto both body and haunch surfaces since decals typically hit the nearest surface. I'm also starting to define cream and warm pale tones for the belly and back fur shading.

I'll apply the warm peach wash to the dorsal normals facing up, keeping the sides and tail cream with crimson tips, chest white, and legs transitioning to deep crimson-brown socks with zigzag edges up to the knee.

Eyes get amber irises with a plum nose. I'm keeping the flat colour count manageable since paints bake into the texture rather than adding to the count, and paw pads fade into cream-grey-gold claws.

Now I'm working out the path coordinates for the hagoromo scarf ribbons, starting near the neck base and flowing back in an S-curve over the shoulders.

Writing ribbon paint pattern...

Now I'm planning the collar: a loop around the neck with jade beads and gold rings, with the ribbons attaching at the collar sides, plus a neck ruff detail. I'm also working out the joint naming scheme for the skeleton hierarchy—hips, spine chain, neck segments, head, jaw, ears, and tail chains—making sure the auto-generated chain names stay distinct and unambiguous.

For the tail chain, I'm settling on a naming pattern like `tail${i}_${k}` to keep names valid and recognizable to a rigger, since something like "tail3" needs to read clearly. For the legs, I'm mapping out named joints like shoulder, elbow, wrist, ball, and toe per limb, figuring out how many points and spans each chain needs so the tip joint gets its own name too.

I'm defining front and hind leg naming (shoulderL/elbowL/wristL/ballL/toeL vs hipHL/kneeHL/hockHL/ballHL/toeHL), setting their parent joints (hind to hips, front to the last spine joint), and now sketching radius arrays that taper along each leg mesh for a natural leg shape.

I'm sizing the paw tube so it ends in a rounded cap near the ground, checking that the foot target height roughly matches the radius so the toe sinks just slightly into the floor plane. Now I'm positioning haunch mass spheres at the hind leg roots, scaling and offsetting them down and back from the hip joint to add visual bulk.

I'm adding elbow/shoulder spheres and checking they sit inside the body wall without clipping, then scattering fur ruff cards on the backs of the legs filtered by normal direction so they only appear facing backward. I'm also making sure the tail's paint sweep uses the same cel-shaded fur edge logic as the rest of the body, and setting up the tail rings so each one rides a bone along a closed catmull curve for a smooth fan shape.

Now I'm scattering fur tuft cards along each tail surface with controlled spacing, size, lean, and bend, oriented along the tail's tangent direction so they flow naturally, with each tail producing its own pair of textured meshes. I'm also setting up the chest ruff by scattering cards over the neck and chest region, filtering by position and normal angle so the tufts only appear on the throat and underside areas.

Now I'm starting to write the full component file, importing the builder, frame, math helpers, path utilities, limb IK, paint/gradient tools, toon shading kit, glow kit, and texture helpers, then defining the cream and peach color palette for the fur.

Defining more colors...

Setting up paint variants...

Defining more coat colors...

Adjusting teeth marching to use a diagonal direction vector combining x and z so fur variation appears on both legs' side and front faces. For hind leg socks I'll push the level up near the hock area, and for ear paint I'll set the inner face as peach pink and outer back as crimson, deciding the split using the face normal's z component.

Now I'm sketching the ear outline with a defined base width and height, placing points counterclockwise to form a tapered, slightly curved shape with a sharp tip, then plotting a smaller inner-ear patch offset toward the front face using a shrinking width condition based on height.

Writing paint function for ear shading...

I'll wrap the ear paint in a cel shader so it responds to light direction properly, and skip extra tuft cards in favor of a few cream spike shapes near the inner ear base. For the skull and other head parts, I'm attaching them all to the head bone and positioning each with scaled sphere geometry relative to a head center reference point.

For face coloring I'm blending cream fur edges on the cheeks with the body's continuous coat tone on top of the head, while the muzzle gets its own cream-white sweep geometry built from a two-point polyline with tapering radius along the bone direction. I'll skip the mouth line for now and move on to adding the nose, lower jaw, and fang-shaped teeth cones on each side.

Positioning the small white fangs at the lower edge of the muzzle so they point downward and peek out just slightly past the jawline for a cute effect, nudging them outward so they don't overlap the lower jaw geometry. I'm skipping the tongue, then sketching three whisker sweeps per side as thin tapered beziers extending outward and back from the muzzle, though I realize cream-colored whiskers would vanish against the cream fur so I need to reconsider the color.

Settling on a warm gold tone for the whiskers to give them an elegant, kitsune-like accent instead of lavender or peach. Now I'm moving on to the facial markings, planning to lay them out as a decal surface across the skull and muzzle with a local coordinate mapping, using a 200x160 SVG viewBox centered at (100,80) where one unit equals 0.001 meters.

I'm placing the eye centers symmetrically at roughly x=45 and x=155, y≈70, then sketching a diamond-shaped forehead mark in red with a gold center, plus sweeping red "kumadori" cheek strokes extending outward and down from the outer eye corners toward the face edges, along with a short under-eye line and tiny gold eyebrow dot accents for a stylized fox-anime look.

I'm adding a thin tapered crimson bridge line running from the forehead mark down between the eyes toward the nose, double-checking decal lift values so the eyes and face markings don't z-fight (giving eyes a slightly higher lift than the marks), and confirming the markings are drawn symmetrically so no mirroring step is needed before positioning the ear joints relative to the head.

Adjusting the ear direction vectors...

Working out the orthogonal basis vectors and computing their cross product to find the thickness axis direction...

Checking that the ear orientation flips correctly for mirrored sides, with the face normal condition determining where to paint, and then thinking through how joints and bones connect for the neck and head, including how the collar loop cuts through the neck using the joint's normal plane.

Now I'm working out the gold sweep and bead placement for the necklace, counting fourteen jade spheres along the loop, then figuring out where the loop's parameter corresponds to the throat point so the pendant hangs correctly given the neck's forward-leaning bone direction.

Attaching the bell pendant and tassels at the throat point, offset downward in world space, and anchoring them to the nearest neck joint. Then setting up bangle loops at the leg joints -- front wrists and hind hocks -- sweeping gold rings around each.

Instead of cutting right at the hock joint, I'll place the bangle plane mid-lower-leg using a chain frame at roughly 62% down the leg, which better follows the tangent there. Skipping elbow tufts for now, but keeping the back-of-leg fur cards. For the nine tails, I'm checking their spatial reach -- base position, horizontal extension, and how far back the overall length stretches from the nose.

Now I'm working out the overall body proportions: hip-to-chest span, neck and head height with ears, and especially the center tail's trajectory using its base and tangent vectors to find where it peaks before the flame tip adds extra height, landing total figure height around 1.9 units.

Now I'm computing the outer tails at their splayed angles, deriving base and tangent direction vectors for the ±75° side tails so their curves match the center tail's proportions while fanning outward.

Checking the spacing, the tails would overlap too heavily and merge into a fluffy mass rather than reading as a distinct fan, so I need to shrink the radius to around 0.085 and narrow the spread angle to roughly ±82° to keep adjacent tails from crowding at greater distances from the base.

I'm also adding stagger by varying tail lengths and base elevations slightly, alternating lateral z-offsets for odd-indexed tails, and giving each tail a tapering radius profile along its length so the fan reads as three-dimensional rather than flat.

Now I'm thinking through fur card detail per tail—roughly 36 cards each, keeping triangle count manageable across all tails—and settling the rest pose for the legs, including shoulder root positions relative to body center height.

Next I'm working out the hip joint path and the spine chain leading from hips through the chest, setting radii at each point, then continuing that same spine curve up through the neck joints toward the head, tapering the radius as it rises and checking how the neck-to-chest transition blends.

Now I'm placing the head joint and skull geometry, figuring out ear and tail positions above it, then sketching out floating foxfire orb positions scattered around the body at varying heights and radii to decide how many to keep and where they look best.

Writing spark placement logic...

I'm shaping the flame cards with a tapered teardrop profile, using varying radii along the sweep so the base is wide and rounded while the tip comes to a point.

For color, I'm giving the body a cyan glow and considering whether to layer a brighter core inside, though it may not be necessary since the card flames already overlap the 3D teardrop shape for added depth. For the tail flames, I'm thinking about adding a main flame plus a smaller secondary wisp slightly offset for variation.

Rigging the glowing tail flames to bend with each tail tip bone, I'm now sketching the gold forehead crest as a diamond-lotus outline with alternating sharp and rounded points to give it a crown-like silhouette.

Still working out the orientation vectors...

For the gem, I'm leaning toward a cyan glow ("#33d6ff") on the forehead to tie it visually to the spirit flames rather than a plain ruby.

Now I'm working out the cheek tufts as bezier spikes sweeping from skull hit points at specific angles, with cream coloring and a tapered tip, plus a larger cream chest tuft for the neck/body area and ring-shaped claw spikes around the toe tips.

Positioning claw spikes manually at the toe-tip frame...

I'll skip toe bean details, then set up scattered belly fluff cards that flow backward and downward where the normal points downward enough. Now I'm working out the hagoromo ribbon chain, anchoring its root near the collar/lower neck and plotting a path of points sweeping outward and down along the side, checking it doesn't collide with the tails positioned further out.

Since the ribbon keeps colliding with the outer tail's region, I'm rerouting it to curl more upward and outward instead, shortening its reach and giving it a bigger wave so it floats alongside the neck like a blowing scarf rather than trailing straight back, adjusting the points to rise and curve back up toward the end.

Setting up ribbon width and a tapering radius function, giving it a tentacle-like chain structure with a box cross-section, and sketching out gold trim sectors for the flat faces -- though since the chain's orientation doesn't align with world-up, I'll skip the sector approach and instead paint gold dashes and end tips using a pattern based on position along the strand.

I'm working out body decal placement for the swirl design, figuring out mirroring logic so the pattern reads consistently whether viewed from the +X or -X side -- using the cross product of forward and up to determine which direction is "head" versus "tail," then flipping the mirror flag accordingly to keep the design symmetric across both sides of the body.

Writing SVG code...

I need the markings to stay clear of the eye shapes, sized around 55 by 75 units, and mapped properly onto the curved skull surface so the decal lines up with the sides at the correct width.

For the eye decal, I'm placing it on the skull surface using a hit position and mirroring based on side, keeping the ink in a plum tone for the lashes.

Now I'm sketching the flame tongue SVG path with its violet outer silhouette...

Adding the small side tongue shapes, then settling on a color palette: a violet-leaning purple outer flame, a bright cyan mid layer, and a pale near-white inner core for contrast against the cream background.

Since the tail chain has no named tip, I'll reference the last joint in the tail array for the bone attachment instead. For the orb flame, I'm layering spheres for a hitodama effect — an outer violet glow shell with an inner cyan-white core, deciding whether to keep it simple with just nested spheres rather than adding extra card shells.

Designing the sparkle cards as small 4-point star shapes anchored near each orb, using pale cyan coloring for a crisp glint effect.

Then I'm working through joint construction for the jaw, defining its pivot point and aim direction relative to the head, and sketching the sweep geometry from the jaw joint down to the chin tip.

Nose placed slightly forward and down from the muzzle tip. I'm checking the neck ruff scatter, confirming the scatter filter has the right vector and normal attributes, and verifying the leg sweeps cover the full chain to the toe with proper radii tapering down to the paw. I'm also working out haunch, shoulder, and elbow tuft placement, starting with the front leg shoulder joint position.

Now I'm pinning down leg chain parameters: front legs root near the shoulder with a toe target forward and down, segment lengths for upper arm, forearm, pastern, and paw, plus bend directions so the elbow kicks back and the wrist angles forward in a natural zigzag given the overall vertical and horizontal span. For the hind legs I'm setting a similar root-to-toe target further back, with segment lengths for thigh, shin, hock, and paw to get the hock angled appropriately behind the body.

Writing tail curve math...

Building the bezier curve path...

Still defining the fur edge tangent logic...

Confirming the shadow color input type checks out, and reusing the body's lit/shadow coat paints for the tail base peach-cream gradient instead of defining new ones. For the gold rings, I'm working out a radius interpolation function that smoothly maps chain position to band size across keyed radii values.

Writing gold ring band code...

For the sweep caps, since the path is closed the ring is welded with no exposed ends. I'm placing two gold rings per tail—a thicker cuff near the base and a thinner ring further out—skipping the idea of a hanging tassel to keep things simpler. I'll move on to the decal code next, accepting it may be heavy on typechecking.

Now I'm working out the small gold ear cuff: a thin torus positioned at the ear's outer edge, figuring out how to orient it relative to the ear's local coordinate frame so it wraps naturally around the edge point.

I'm placing the torus cuff using the ear's local frame and y-direction, then adding a dangling tassel card hanging below it with bead accents, two tassels total. I should also consider adding a small flame or tomoe spirit marking elsewhere on the design.

Now I'm starting the actual builder code, defining the hips joint as the root with its position and orientation, then setting up the spine chain starting from that same point using a catmull curve with a few joints marked with the spine role.
